kids.content: When r = 1 , M (1 , L, c 2 ) is isomorphic to S [ c 2 ] , the Hilbert scheme of 0 -dimensional closed subschemes in S of length c 2 . Fogarty showed that S [ n ] ( n ∈ Z ≥ 0 ) is a smooth projective variety of dimension 2 n [ Fog68 ] and computed its Picard group [ Fog73 ]. The Betti numbers of S [ n ] were completely determined by Göttsche [ G ¨ 90 ]. When r ≥ 2 , M ( r, L, c 2 ) can be reducible or non-reduced. But starting from Donaldson’s generic smoothness result [ Don90 ], the study of M ( r, L, c 2 ) has revealed that M ( r, L, c 2 ) has better geometric properties as we ﬁx r ≥ 2 , L , and let c 2 increase. For example, when c 2 is large enough, Gieseker–Li [ GL94 ] [ GL96 ] and O’Grady [ O’G96 ] showed that M ( r, L, c 2 ) is irreducible, normal, and generically smooth of expected dimension. Some asymptotic phenomena also occur in the Picard group and Betti numbers of M ( r, L, c ) ( r ≥ 2 ) [ Qin92 ][ Li96 ][ Li97 ][ CW22 ].
Question 1.1. Are there asymptotic phenomena similar to those above in the geometry of M ( r, L, c 2 ) when r = 0 ?

Sheaves on S of rank zero are supported on points or curves. In this paper, we focus on those pure sheaves supported on curves, which are called one-dimensional sheaves. In contrast to the positive rank case, there are few general results for the moduli space of one-dimensional sheaves. An essential diﬃculty is that the supports of one-dimensional sheaves can be singular, even non-reduced. To distinguish this case, we use the following notation. Given a nonzero eﬀective divisor β on S and an integer χ , denote by M β,χ the moduli space parametrizing polystable one-dimensional sheaves F on S , with determinant det( F ) ∼ = O S ( β ) and Euler characteristic χ ( F ) = χ . We will make the following assumption on β , unless otherwise stated.

kids.content: A conjecture [ SZ24 , Conjecture 1.3] was proposed on the stabilization of (intersection cohomology) Betti numbers of M β,χ when χ is ﬁxed and β is suﬃciently positive, as an analogue of [ CW22 , Conjecture 1.1]. When S is a del Pezzo surface, this conjecture was resolved in [ PSSZ24 ] by proving an asymptotic formula of the reﬁned BPS invariants which also reﬁne the Betti numbers.

The primary motivation of this paper is to explore the stabilization of the Picard number ρ ( M β,χ ) of M β,χ when β is suﬃciently positive. Here, the Picard number ρ ( X ) of a proper scheme X is deﬁned as the dimension of the Q -vector space Num Q ( X ) of the numerically equivalence classes of line bundles on X with rational coeﬃcients, in the sense of [ Kle66 ].
